title: Tonight, a solar storm hits Earth

scenes.text: Tonight, a Carrington-size solar storm hits Earth.
The Sun throws a giant cloud of plasma straight at us.
It arrives in a day or two.
The sky lights up. Auroras glow far from the poles.
Satellites could be damaged, and GPS could fail.
Power grids could overload, and blackouts could last for weeks.
In 1859, the real one set telegraph lines sparking.
In 1989, a smaller storm blacked out Quebec for nine hours.
But here's the twist. In 2012, one just as big missed Earth by about a week.
